findings.issue: Eight `_of_isOpen` wrappers (lines 79, 122, 149, 167, 183, 199, 216, 233) take `IsOpen Ω` + `a ∈ Ω`, strictly stronger than the `Ω ∈ 𝓝 a` of the general theorem sitting directly above each one; every body is just `general (hΩopen.mem_nhds ha) ...`. This is special-case duplication of the whole API at a lower level of generality, with no in-repo use (grep shows no file outside this one mentions any of these names) and no roadmap need (PDE Lane C.13–14 ask for the maximum principles and Harnack, not hypothesis-format variants). Mathlib does not ship both an `s ∈ 𝓝 a` and an `IsOpen s`/`a ∈ s` form of the same theorem.

findings.issue: `eqOn_const_of_harmonicOnNhd_of_isLocalMaxOn` (177) and `..._isLocalMinOn` (193) are not more general than the `IsLocalMax`/`IsLocalMin` versions they call: under the theorem's own `hΩa : Ω ∈ 𝓝 a`, `𝓝[Ω] a = 𝓝 a`, so `IsLocalMaxOn f Ω a ↔ IsLocalMax f a`. They duplicate the API with an equivalent hypothesis, one `IsLocalMaxOn.isLocalMax hΩa` from the existing statement.

summary: Eight new `_of_isOpen` theorems restate existing results with the strictly stronger hypothesis `IsOpen Ω ∧ a ∈ Ω` in place of `Ω ∈ 𝓝 a`, with bodies that are a single `IsOpen.mem_nhds` application and no in-repo consumer; the `IsLocalMaxOn`/`IsLocalMinOn` forms are equivalent, not more general, under the `Ω ∈ 𝓝 a` hypothesis the theorem already carries. Only the nonneg dichotomy is new content.
